title: Constant local fibre dimension near one Cohen-Macaulay fibre stalk
statement: Let f:X→T be a scheme morphism [def-pc-scheme], U an open of T such that f restricted over U is flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] and locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], and W an open of X. Let y∈W with f(y)∈U. Suppose the depth [def-weil-pbc-depth] of the fibre local ring at y [def-pc-scheme-fibre; def-weil-pbc-module-stalk] equals its ring Krull dimension [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. There exist n∈ℕ and an open O of X with y∈O⊆W such that every z∈O has local topological fibre dimension [def-kun-topological-dimension-at-point] n. No Cohen-Macaulay assumption is imposed away from y; no partition is asserted.

source.place: Tag 00RH (Lemma 10.130.4), its proof using 00QE, 00RE, 00R7, 00RC; Tag 0A21 (10); local step underlying 02NM

proof.text: Work in the source open W intersected with the inverse image of U. Choose affine neighbourhoods of f(y) in U and y in this source open. Their ring map R to S is flat and finitely presented. The fibre local ring at the prime q of y is the given fibre stalk, so hdepth makes it Cohen-Macaulay. Its local relative dimension n is a natural number, since the fibre is locally of finite type over a field. Tag 0A21 (10) identifies this relative dimension with local topological fibre dimension. The proof of Tag 00RH gives an open neighbourhood of q where that relative dimension is n: after a principal shrinking choose a quasi-finite map R[t_1,...,t_n] to S. On the fibre its target local ring is Cohen-Macaulay and its source is regular, so the fibre map is flat (00RE). Fibrewise flatness (00R7) gives flatness of the polynomial map at q. Openness of flatness (00RC) gives a further principal shrinking on which it is flat. At every point of this shrinking, base change makes the corresponding fibre map flat and quasi-finite over polynomial n-space. The local dimension formula therefore gives relative dimension n at every point (again 00RE). The image O of this principal affine open is open in X, contains y, and lies in W. Open fibre inclusions and the residue-field restriction isomorphisms preserve local topological dimension, giving the equality for all z in O. Only the fibre stalk at y is assumed Cohen-Macaulay; no partition is used. The cited dimension-at-point formula supplies finiteness and the local-ring-plus-residue-transcendence-degree equality. Quasi-finite polynomial factorization is the cited 00QE node. Its fibre residue extension is finite, so the transcendence degrees agree and the zero-dimensional fibre makes the local ring dimensions equal; this verifies the additive dimension hypothesis of the cited miracle-flatness node (00R4). The fibrewise-flatness and openness steps are the cited 00R7 and 00RC nodes. These are dependencies of the natural-language plan; the Lean theorem remains the single named sorry, not a claim that its algebraic-to-scheme transport has been formalized.

theorem exists_constant_fibre_dimension_neighbourhood_of_depth_eq_ringKrullDim
    {X T : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ T) (U : T.Opens)
    [Flat (f ∣_ U)] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation (f ∣_ U)] (W : X.Opens)
    (y : X) (hy : y ∈ W) (ht : f y ∈ U)
    (hdepth :
      (IsLocalRing.depth (R := (f.fiber (f y)).presheaf.stalk (f.asFiber y))
        ((f.fiber (f y)).presheaf.stalk (f.asFiber y)) : WithBot ℕ∞) =
          ringKrullDim ((f.fiber (f y)).presheaf.stalk (f.asFiber y))) :
    ∃ (n : ℕ) (O : X.Opens), y ∈ O ∧ O ≤ W ∧
      ∀ z ∈ O, topologicalKrullDimAt (f.asFiber z) = (n : WithBot ℕ∞)
